themes_detail.label: Animal infestation surge
themes_detail.summary: Unsanitary animal complaints on private property spiked to 5 complaints THIS WEEK versus a baseline of 0.2 per week over the prior 8 weeks—a 1900% increase (z-score: 10.97)—suggesting a rapid outbreak of rodents or other pests that aligns with the Community Board's long-standing request for pest control funding.
evidence: 5 unsanitary animal complaints THIS WEEK vs. 0.2 weekly average over prior 8 weeks (1900% spike, z-score: 10.97)
Community Board has repeatedly requested animal and pest control funding from Department of Health and Mental Hygiene, indicating chronic neighborhood problem
Spike is statistically significant and emerged abruptly, not a gradual trend
reporting_angles: Interview residents in buildings with multiple complaints; investigate whether this is tied to construction or waste management changes
Reach out to NYC Department of Health to ask whether they have detected a surge in rodent/pest complaints across Manhattan or just this district

themes_detail.label: Commercial noise explosion
themes_detail.summary: Commercial noise complaints surged to 93 THIS WEEK compared to a baseline of 23.9 per week over the prior 8 weeks—a 290% spike (z-score: 5.75)—indicating a sudden increase in bar, restaurant, or venue activity or enforcement gaps in Morningside Heights.
evidence: 93 commercial noise complaints THIS WEEK vs. 23.9 weekly average over prior 8 weeks (290% spike, z-score: 5.75)
Noise - Commercial is among top 10 complaint categories by volume (399 total over 90 days), but THIS WEEK's spike represents a discrete, dramatic acceleration
No comparable spike in residential or street/sidewalk noise, suggesting venues or businesses rather than general construction
reporting_angles: Map the 93 complaints to identify which blocks or specific venues are driving the surge; interview neighbors about late-night activity
Contact 311 and Precinct 26 to ask whether any new bars, nightlife venues, or events opened recently or whether enforcement efforts changed

themes_detail.label: Elevator failures mounting
themes_detail.summary: Elevator complaints jumped to 33 (or 6, depending on categorization) LAST WEEK versus a baseline of 7.9 (or 1.8) per week over the prior 8 weeks—a 319% to 243% increase (z-scores: 5.53–5.13)—affecting residents in a high-rise district and potentially indicating deferred maintenance or aging infrastructure.
evidence: 33 elevator complaints LAST WEEK vs. 7.9 weekly average over prior 8 weeks (319% spike, z-score: 5.53) — or 6 complaints vs. 1.8 average (243% spike, z-score: 5.13) depending on categorization
Morningside Heights / Hamilton Heights is a multi-story residential district with aging buildings, making elevator failures a direct quality-of-life issue
Spike emerged suddenly LAST WEEK and persists, not a gradual trend
reporting_angles: Identify which buildings generated the elevator complaints; investigate whether they share common issues (same contractor, age of systems, deferred maintenance)
Interview building managers and residents about whether this reflects a backlog of maintenance post-pandemic or new inspector scrutiny

themes_detail.label: Sanitation collection collapse
themes_detail.summary: Missed collection complaints surged to 4 LAST WEEK versus a baseline of 0.2 per week over the prior 8 weeks—a 1500% spike (z-score: 8.66)—and aligns with the Community Board's recurring budget request for more sanitation trucks and equipment.
evidence: 4 missed collection complaints LAST WEEK vs. 0.2 weekly average over prior 8 weeks (1500% spike, z-score: 8.66)

Community Board has repeatedly submitted budget requests for 'new or increased number of sanitation trucks and other equipment' to Department of Sanitation, indicating longstanding resource constraints
Spike is concurrent with unusual animal complaints (pests), suggesting possible cascading sanitation failures
reporting_angles: Contact NYC Department of Sanitation to ask whether District 109 lost routes, sanitation workers, or truck availability LAST WEEK
Canvass residential blocks to verify whether garbage is piling up and whether residents attribute it to service cuts or holiday scheduling

themes_detail.label: Outside building code complaints
themes_detail.summary: Complaints tagged 'Outside Building' jumped to 4 LAST WEEK versus a baseline of 0.8 per week over the prior 8 weeks—a 433% spike (z-score: 7.51)—potentially indicating exterior facade, entrance, or structural issues requiring Department of Buildings scrutiny.
evidence: 4 'Outside Building' complaints LAST WEEK vs. 0.8 weekly average over prior 8 weeks (433% spike, z-score: 7.51)
355 DOB alteration permits filed in last 90 days (315 alterations), suggesting active renovation work; spike may reflect incomplete or unsafe exterior work
Spike is isolated to this category and week, suggesting a discrete event or batch of complaints
reporting_angles: Query DOB data to identify which buildings received recent alteration permits and map them to the 4 'Outside Building' complaints from LAST WEEK
Contact DOB to ask whether inspectors are flagging incomplete or unsafe exterior work on Columbia University–affiliated or privately owned properties
